open_items: Seen, not verifiable: https://aimewebapp.blob.core.windows.net/finalactions/06o2263.pdf (scanned; the host answers robots.txt with 400, so quotecheck will not fetch it). Ordinance 06-O-2263 (Z-06-111), adopted 2007-02-05, rezoned 84, 88, 96, 98, 100, 120 and 130 Poole Creek Road and 3715 and 3711 Wilson Drive from I-1 and R-4 to I-1-C, with conditions on truck route signs (I-75/Central Ave/Crown Rd or I-85/Jonesboro Rd to Southside Industrial Park Drive), coordination with the Atlanta Police Department on driveways near the Atlanta Police Academy, and Wilson Road right-of-way and widening. The GIS layer lists the result as I-1, not I-1-C. This is the neighbouring tract, not 81 Poole Creek Rd: ask whether similar truck-route expectations would be put on this parcel.
Check the City's adopted Comprehensive Development Plan text and the NPU Z neighbourhood plans for this area; only the GIS future-land-use layer was read.

claims.text: Sewer: the City of Atlanta Sewer Pipe layer (MapEGIS/manholes layer 1), asked for pipes within 1,200 ft of the parcel's map point that are not marked abandoned, returns 8-inch Active Public lines on Poole Creek Rd (the parcel's frontage road), upstream street numbers 44 to 183, installed 1956.
The layer's own code list: SERVSTAT APUB means Active Public and ABAN means Abandoned.

Within 600 ft of the parcel's map point the same layer shows only abandoned 8-inch 1958 lines under Gilbert Wy, Archcrest Dr and Celeste Dr SE: streets of a former residential layout, on or right beside the parcel.

open_items: Water: no public City of Atlanta water-main layer was found (the watershed GIS folders answered empty and the capital-projects service was not started), so water is unknown and the verdict is unknown though sewer is shown nearby. Ask Atlanta Department of Watershed Management for the nearest water main and its size.
Sewer capacity: the active lines found are 8-inch, 1950s, in the Poole Creek Rd frontage; only the utility can say whether they can take an industrial building's flow.

The abandoned 1958 street sewers (Gilbert Wy, Archcrest Dr, Celeste Dr) suggest the parcel was once a platted residential subdivision. Ask the title examiner whether those streets were formally closed and the old lots combined, and look on site for old foundations or fill.

open_items: A web search for the site address found no sale notice, public notice or development-authority release; listing sites were not checked (CoStar, LoopNet and Crexi are excluded by rule). Ask a broker or the owner whether the land is offered or committed.

Same owner for 19 years (sale 2007-11-15), months after the neighbouring tract was rezoned I-1-C for a developer (06-O-2263, February 2007): ask whether this parcel was bought as part of that project and whether a site plan or option exists.

The owner on the assessor roll is an entity with 'ET AL' (more than one owner on title). The Georgia Secretary of State search is a known wall (403); a person should look up the entity's status, formation date, principal office and registered agent by hand.

Ask whether the owner is affiliated with the railroad whose line runs 419 ft from the parcel (the brief); a railroad-related holder may sell only with rail-use terms or not at all. Not checked: no search by owner name was made, by rule.
Pull recent deeds: the brief's last sale is 2007-11-15 for $4,718,631.
